samples.summary: Rerun's loop-status update runs on the refused (fork / unmanaged) path and posts a false status
samples.evidence: The `Clear the block and re-run CI` step returns early with an `outcome` of "⚠️ `@claude rerun` only works on same-repo agent-managed PRs…" for a fork or an unmanaged PR (agent-rerun.yml:126-131) — no latches are deleted, no label dropped, no CI re-run. The new `Update loop status (rerun)` step (line 227) has NO `if:` gating on that outcome (unlike every other new call site, e.g. agent-fix.yml:529 gates on `steps.eligible.outputs.eligible == 'true'`), so it still runs and writes `--note "A maintainer ran @claude rerun — paged latches cleared, agent:blocked dropped, CI re-running; the review-fix round budget restarts from here."`. On an unmanaged/fork PR this creates a brand-new bot dashboard comment asserting three things that provably did not happen. The `--event rerun` headline ("loop re-engaged — CI re-running") compounds it. It should be gated on the managed path (e.g. a new step output from the clear step).

samples.summary: Sticky-comment upsert can overwrite or delete a maintainer's comment that quotes the dashboard
samples.evidence: `isOwnStatusComment` (line 114) returns true for ANY comment containing `<!-- agent-loop-status -->` whose author is a trusted human (`TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS` = OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, line 81/88), not just our bot. GitHub's "Quote reply" copies the RAW markdown of a comment, HTML comments included, so a maintainer quoting the dashboard produces a comment that satisfies the predicate. The upsert then treats it as one of ours: `fresh` is sorted by id ascending and `fresh[0]` is PATCHed with the freshly rendered body (line 440-447) while `fresh.slice(1)` is DELETED (line 448-455). If the bot's own comment was deleted/edited away, `fresh[0]` is the maintainer's comment and their text is overwritten; otherwise their quote-reply is the younger entry and is deleted outright. Either way human-authored content is destroyed by a display-only projection. The predicate should require the bot logins (or additionally require the body to start with the marker as this renderer emits it).

samples.summary: `ready` is derived from draft state and outranks the caller's event, mislabelling a promoted PR that re-entered a fix round
samples.evidence: main() computes `ready = flags.event === 'promoted' || (prView.isDraft === false && headRefName.startsWith('agent/'))` (line 395-397), and `renderLoopStatus` gives `ready` precedence over `EVENT_HEADLINE[event]` (line 240-244) and over the newest row's "Then" cell, which becomes "🤝 promoted" (line 277-278). Once an agent PR has been promoted it is no longer a draft forever after, so any later round on it — a maintainer push, `@claude fix`, or a new panel round that sets `blocked=true` — renders the headline "ready for human review" and the newest round as "🤝 promoted" while the `Latest:` note directly under it says e.g. "Panel requested changes…" or "dispatching fix round 2 of 3". The projection then contradicts itself precisely in the situation a human is reading it. `ready` should be scoped to the promotion event (or at least yield to a blocked/fix-dispatched event).

samples.summary: Display rendering runs BEFORE the PROCEED decision output, so a renderer throw would suppress the fixer dispatch
samples.evidence: At the end of the guard: `setOutput("verdict", guardVerdictLine(verdict)); appendStepSummary(renderGuardSummary(verdict)); setOutput("proceed", "true");` (lines 296-298). `guardVerdictLine`/`renderGuardSummary` are unguarded calls, so any throw in them exits the script non-zero with `proceed` never written — the fix round is not dispatched and the guard step reds. This inverts the ordering rule this very change states for the CI arm ("Summary writes are FAIL-SAFE and always AFTER the outputs of the branch they describe", agent-iterate-ci.yml:147-152) and the rule asserted in guard-verdict.mjs's own header ("a bug in this file can mislabel a decision but never change one"). `page()` gets this right (setOutput paged/proceed first, line 96-97); the proceed path does not. Move `setOutput("proceed","true")` above the two render calls, or wrap them in try/catch.

samples.summary: `AFTER="$(git ls-remote …)"` under `set -eo pipefail` aborts the step, making the intended empty-AFTER fallback unreachable
samples.evidence: Both new outcome steps compute `AFTER="$(git ls-remote origin "refs/heads/$BRANCH" | cut -f1)"` and then branch on `-n "$AFTER"` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:432-439, agent-review-panel.yml:1756-1763). GitHub's default shell is `bash -e -o pipefail`, so a failing `git ls-remote` (network error, deleted branch) fails the assignment and terminates the step before the `else` branch can run. The step is `continue-on-error`, so the consequence is that the sticky comment is silently left claiming the previous state (e.g. "🔧 fixer running…") in exactly the failure case the `-n` guard was written to cover. Adding `|| true` to the substitution (or `AFTER=$(… ) || AFTER=""`) restores the intended fallback.

samples.summary: On-demand-fix status update cannot achieve its stated purpose — the paged latch it is meant to supersede is never cleared
samples.evidence: The step's comment says it exists because "an on-demand fix can push a commit (new round) on a PR whose dashboard still says 'paged'". But `@claude fix` does not delete the `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` / `<!-- agent-paged -->` latches (only agent-rerun.yml does, agent-rerun.yml:141-147), and `renderLoopStatus` gives a detected latch absolute precedence: headline "🛑 paged to a human" and newest-round cell "🛑 paged" (loop-status.mjs:240-244, 274-276). So after a successful on-demand fix the dashboard still reads paged and still contradicts the outcome comment; only the `Latest:` note changes. The step is not wrong, but it does not fix the stated problem.

samples.summary: "Other checks" cell counts every non-lens github-actions check run, and treats `cancelled` as red
samples.evidence: `buildRounds` takes `others = runs.filter(r => !names.has(r.name))` over ALL github-actions check runs on the commit (line 139/154) and marks the cell ❌ when any of them has a conclusion in `RED_CONCLUSIONS` (line 121/157), which includes `cancelled`. Those runs include the agent pipeline's own jobs, and agent-review-panel.yml sets `cancel-in-progress: true` on its concurrency group (line 116-118), so a superseded panel run leaves cancelled check runs on the commit and the table will show CI as ❌ for a round whose CI was green. The column is labelled "Other checks" next to a Review-panel column, so a reader will read it as CI status.

samples.summary: The displayed fix-round budget is computed from different inputs per arm, so the same sticky comment oscillates
samples.evidence: `countFailedReviewRounds` is called with the caller's `--required-checks` when supplied and the full lens manifest otherwise (line 386-390), and the cap comes only from `--max-rounds`. The panel/promote/fix arms pass both (agent-review-panel.yml:1449-1450, 1285-1286, 1765-1766); the CI arm (agent-iterate-ci.yml:440), the on-demand fix arm (agent-fix.yml:536) and the rerun arm (agent-rerun.yml:234) pass NEITHER. Because the body is re-derived in full each update, the single sticky comment flips between "**Fix rounds used:** 2 of 3" and "**Fix rounds used:** 2" (and potentially a different count, since the manifest is a superset of required_checks) purely according to which arm wrote last — the budget line a human is meant to trust changes meaning without any state change.

samples.summary: lensCell drops the passed count when a round has failures AND pending lenses
samples.evidence: `const rest = pending.length > 0 ? `, ${pending.length} ⏳` : passed.length > 0 ? ` (${passed.length} ✅)` : "";` — the ternary is exclusive, so a round with 1 failed, 2 pending and 3 passed renders "❌ x, 2 ⏳" and silently omits the 3 ✅. Cheap to make additive.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. agent-rerun.yml:126-131 returns early on the fork/unmanaged path having done nothing (no latch deletion at 137-147, no removeLabel at 159, no reRunWorkflow at 179), setting only `outcome` and no `managed` output. The `Update loop status (rerun)` step at agent-rerun.yml:227-237 has only `continue-on-error: true` and NO `if:` gate, and the rerun step does not setFailed, so the step executes on that refused path with `--event rerun` and a note asserting "paged latches cleared, agent:blocked dropped, CI re-running". loop-status.mjs:215 maps `rerun` to the headline "loop re-engaged — CI re-running" (used whenever paged/ready are false, lines 240-244), the note renders at line 259, and lines 436-459 POST a brand-new comment when no own status comment exists — so an unmanaged/fork PR gets a fabricated dashboard comment asserting three things that did not happen. The comparison call site agent-fix.yml:528-529 does gate its equivalent step; the job holds issues: write (line 59) so the write succeeds; nothing in the route job (lines 23-27, 48) filters fork/unmanaged PRs. Missing guard producing a false state projection is in the correctness lane, and the file's own comments (lines 52-57, 150-156) establish "report what happened, not what was attempted" as the violated invariant.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `isOwnStatusComment` (loop-status.mjs:114-118) requires only that the body contains `<!-- agent-loop-status -->` and that `isTrustedAuthor` (loop-status.mjs:84-89) passes — and that helper returns true for ANY human with author_association OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR (TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS, line 81), not just the bot logins. loop-status.test.mjs:201 pins this: a MEMBER human with the marker is treated as "ours". The upsert (loop-status.mjs:436-455) pulls every PR comment via listAllComments (metrics.mjs:859, no author prefilter), filters with that predicate, PATCHes fresh[0] with the rendered dashboard and DELETEs all of fresh.slice(1) (delete errors swallowed at line 452). A maintainer quote-reply copies raw markdown including the HTML comment marker, so it matches `.includes` and is either overwritten or hard-deleted. No guard elsewhere prevents this — the bot-login check at line 87 is an OR branch bypassed by the association branch. Real data-loss/overwrite of human content: blocking under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: `ready` is derived from draft state and outranks the caller's event, mislabelling a promoted PR that re-entered a fix round
finding.evidence: main() computes `ready = flags.event === 'promoted' || (prView.isDraft === false && headRefName.startsWith('agent/'))` (line 395-397), and `renderLoopStatus` gives `ready` precedence over `EVENT_HEADLINE[event]` (line 240-244) and over the newest row's "Then" cell, which becomes "🤝 promoted" (line 277-278). Once an agent PR has been promoted it is no longer a draft forever after, so any later round on it — a maintainer push, `@claude fix`, or a new panel round that sets `blocked=true` — renders the headline "ready for human review" and the newest round as "🤝 promoted" while the `Latest:` note directly under it says e.g. "Panel requested changes…" or "dispatching fix round 2 of 3". The projection then contradicts itself precisely in the situation a human is reading it. `ready` should be scoped to the promotion event (or at least yield to a blocked/fix-dispatched event).

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as the finding describes. loop-status.mjs:395-397 derives `ready` from persistent PR state (non-draft + agent/ branch), not from the current event; renderLoopStatus gives `ready` precedence over EVENT_HEADLINE (lines 240-244) and over the newest row's "Then" cell (lines 274-284), while the `--note` is rendered unconditionally at line 259. The post-promotion path is reachable and unguarded: nothing re-drafts a PR (mark-ready.mjs:192,199-203 only flips draft→ready), `@claude fix` has no draft/promotion gate (agent-fix.yml:528-539 with fix-eligible.mjs checking only head verdicts/forks), and the panel gate (agent-review-panel.yml:153-246) admits any non-fork agent/ branch regardless of draft state, later calling loop-status with `--event panel` (line 1014, note "Panel requested changes…") and `--event fix-dispatched` (line 1447). In those runs the projection renders "ready for human review" / "🤝 promoted" directly above a note saying changes were requested or a fix round was dispatched — a self-contradicting projection in exactly the situation a human reads it. The existing test (loop-status.test.mjs:162-167) pins the precedence but only covers the promotion case, so it does not refute the bug. No not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies (this is rendering/state-precedence logic, squarely in the correctness lane).
